record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Construct a simple algorithm that takes an oriented link in the oriented 3-sphere S^3 together with surgery coefficients and outputs a colored graph representing the closed 3-manifold obtained by performing that surgery.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A closed PL 3-manifold M can be represented by a 4-colored graph (also called a crystallization, in the irreducible case), i.e. a finite multigraph G whose edges are properly colored by the set {0,1,2,3} such that every vertex has exactly one edge of each color, with the property that the regular 4-dimensional pseudo-complex K(G) associated to G has |K(G)| ≅ M. By a classical theorem of Lickorish and Wallace, every closed orientable 3-manifold can be obtained from the oriented 3-sphere S^3 by Dehn surgery along an oriented framed link L ⊂ S^3, that is, by an oriented link together with a choice of surgery coefficient (a rational number, or ∞) on each component.

Problem. Construct an explicit, simple algorithm with the following specification:
- Input: an oriented link L in S^3 (given, for instance, by a planar diagram) together with a surgery coefficient assigned to each component of L.
- Output: a 4-colored graph G that represents the closed 3-manifold M obtained from S^3 by performing the prescribed Dehn surgery on L.

The algorithm should be combinatorial and effective, taking only the link diagram and the surgery coefficients as data and producing the edge-colored graph directly, without first passing through an arbitrary triangulation or handle decomposition of M.
artifact.status_search_result: Algorithms producing edge-colored graphs from framed links exist: there are constructions yielding 4-colored graphs representing the 3-manifold obtained by integer Dehn surgery on a framed link in S^3, as well as 5-colored graphs representing the associated bounded 4-manifolds from Kirby diagrams. These results address the integer-surgery (and dotted-component) case, but a simple unified algorithm handling arbitrary rational surgery coefficients does not appear in fully explicit form in the standard literature, so the problem can be regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: From framed links to crystallizations of bounded 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm from framed links to crystallizations of bounded 4-manifolds, whose boundary is the 3-manifold obtained by surgery.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic constructions from framed links to colored graphs are known.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams and 5-colored graphs representing compact 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Construct a 5-colored graph representing a 4-manifold directly from a planar diagram of a framed link.
status_evidence.claim: Procedures from link diagrams to colored graphs in the related 4-dimensional setting are explicit.

status_evidence.title: Dotted Links, Heegaard Diagrams, and Colored Graphs for PL 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: 4-colored graphs representing 3-manifolds obtained from S^3 by Dehn surgery along a framed link.
status_evidence.claim: Existing methods translate framed link surgery descriptions into 4-colored graphs.
